load.energy_growth_note: The IRP shows peak forecasts only as charts (Charts 12-13), with no tables, so no peak numbers are recorded here. Growth is attributed to large new industrial loads, chemical and crypto-mining customers. By 2026, industrial is forecast at 49% of energy sales, more than 10 points above the 2023 mix. The 2024 stakeholder slides tabulate seasonal capacity balance: summer deficit 802 MW in 2028, 1,049 MW in 2035, 4,099 MW in 2045; winter deficit 1,147 MW in 2028, 4,670 MW in 2045. The IRP text says the need could exceed 8,300 MW by 2045 in the high-load future. The Jun 2026 Mid-Cycle says load is tracking the IRP's Future 2 (reference) forecast.
load.large_load_notes: Mid-Cycle (Jun 2026): EAL signed agreements with Avaio, Google and others for about 1 GW of new supply in the past 12 months. That figure is not data centers only. AVAIO Digital 'Leo' campus in Pulaski County near Wrightsville/Little Rock: 150 MW contracted from about Jun 30, 2027, potentially up to 1 GW, needing two new 115 kV lines.

load.energy_growth_note: No system-wide peak forecast was found, so per-jurisdiction figures are given. irp.next_due: 2027 IRP (OG&E has filed annually in 2024, 2025 and 2026; date not confirmed)

load.energy_growth_note: These are gross summer demand forecasts before DSM; CAGR is computed. Net planning demand rises from 7,811 MW (2028) to 8,746 MW (2036). It is 6,513 MW in 2027 only because 925 MW of load-reduction programs still count as load modifiers that year. Energy grows from 42,404 GWh (2027) to 55,249 GWh (2036), about 3.0%/yr. The commercial class, which includes data centers, jumps from 18,208 GWh (2027) to 27,448 GWh (2035), about +51%. Winter peak forecast: 6,741 to 7,951 MW. Summer capacity need: 976 MW (2028), 1,613 MW (2031), 3,506 MW (2036). Winter need is larger: 1,187 MW (2028/29), 1,922 MW (2031/32), 3,670 MW (2036/37). OG&E set a new all-time peak above 6,800 MW in summer 2026 (secondary: earnings-call summary).
load.large_load_notes: Some individual requests are for hundreds or even thousands of MW; historically most were 50 MW or less. Requests come from manufacturing, refining, federal facilities, data centers and crypto. Only contract-signed large loads are generally included in the forecast. The share of new load from customers of 50 MW or more is confidential. Google: OG&E will serve three new Google data centers in Muskogee and Stillwater. Electric Service Agreements and Capacity Purchase Agreements were announced Apr 30, 2026 and filed at the OCC; MW was not disclosed. OG&E has filed a new large-load tariff.
